_comment: What Unity is told to call, and when.
A [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod] attribute is not enough on its own: in a
player, Unity does not scan assemblies for it. The Editor does that at build
time and writes the result into RuntimeInitializeOnLoads.json, which the
player reads. There is no Editor here, so the list is written by hand and
PlayerImage appends it to the depot's own.
Keeping it beside the source is the point: an entry point that is added to
a .cs file and not to this list is silently never called, which is the
single most confusing way for a patch to fail. The reverse is worse -- an
entry listed here whose patch is wrong runs anyway. Both Addressables
redirects from the old port were deleted for that reason: they pointed the
catalog at persistentDataPath, which is external storage, while PlayerImage
had already rewritten its content root to internal storage at build time.
nameSpace is optional and defaults to none. The ported patches sit in the
global namespace, as the game's own classes do.
